title: Do Not Mess With A Grave (FULL TEXT STORY)
format: Long-form (13m45s) fake-iPhone iMessage screen recording, 360x424 @30fps (near-square ~0.85 aspect, letterboxed on desktop), no narration/no TTS, single looping ambient horror music bed. Category People & Blogs.

title_pattern.notes: Rule-of-the-world warning title ('Do Not...') framed as advice, plus a parenthetical format label '(FULL TEXT STORY)' that targets the text-story audience and signals the compiled long version of a story likely first cut as Shorts. No character, no number, no stakes, no curiosity gap beyond the taboo itself; the channel's other titles follow the same pattern (NEVER RESPOND TO UNKNOWN NUMBERS, MY DAUGHTER IS A GHOST). At 1.03x median it performs exactly at baseline - the title is generic and the taboo (grave) is a stock trope.

thumbnail.composition: One oversized iOS lock-screen notification card spanning the full width (rounded white rectangle, ~45% of frame height) centred slightly below middle on a mottled dark teal/blue grunge texture; 'FULL VIDEO' in heavy white brush-script caps top-right.
thumbnail.text: Notification: app label 'MESSAGES' (grey caps with green Messages icon), sender 'Mason' (bold), body 'We shouldn't have done what we did'. Overlay: 'FULL VIDEO'.
thumbnail.colours: Dark desaturated teal/blue vignette background, pure white card, black SF-style text, iMessage green icon as the only accent; no red, no faces.
thumbnail.subject_scale_contrast: No human subject - the 'subject' is the message itself, blown up so the body text is readable at phone-feed size. Scale contrast is huge card vs. empty dark field; nothing else competes.
thumbnail.why_it_works: Reads instantly as 'a text you weren't meant to see' - a guilty confession with an unexplained 'what we did' (curiosity gap). Familiar iOS UI is legible at tiny size and matches the channel's whole format. Weaknesses (explains baseline performance): no horror imagery at all, nothing tells you it's about a grave, generic 'FULL VIDEO' label, same template on every upload, and the line doesn't appear verbatim in the video.

hook.verbatim_0_5s: [Lock screen, notification from Jason] 'Oh please not this again 😑' -> [chat opens] Mason: 'Guys I don't feel good about what we did yesterday' / Jason: 'Oh please not this again 😑' / 'It was just a dare, a stupid school dare'
hook.visual_0_5s: Fake iPhone lock screen (4:23, Wed Feb 18) with a blurred teen-boy wallpaper and one Messages banner; hard cut at ~3s into the group chat where the first two bubbles are already on screen.
hook.device: Notification cold-open (answer before the question: an exasperated reply implies a recurring guilt) + guilt confession with withheld object ('what we did yesterday') + immediate reveal it was a dare. No narration, no title card - the text IS the hook.
hook.notes: The actual taboo (cracking a tombstone) isn't stated until ~28s, which is slow for a 'Do Not Mess With A Grave' title; viewers who clicked for the grave wait half a minute.

beats.summary: Lock-screen banner shows a friend's exasperated reply ('Oh please not this again') before we see what it answers - implies an ongoing guilt.
Mason says he feels bad about 'what we did yesterday'; friends reveal it was a truth-or-dare: they cracked a tombstone.
Mason insists it was wrong; three friends mock and minimise ('stop acting like we dug up a corpse').
Mason quotes his grandma: disturbing graves brings trouble you don't see coming. Jason (the future first victim) says 'nothing is gonna happen'.
All four had the same nightmare; Mason narrates it in 8 bubbles ending on a hand coming out of the grave; everyone confirms identical details.
Tariq and Lucas explain it away (talked about it for an hour, dreams copy details); Mason pushes back; ends on 'I hope you guys are right. I really do.'
ALL-CAPS 'SOMETHING REALLY BAD HAS HAPPENED' - Jason died in his sleep, no cause. Mason repeats the death details.
Mason links grave -> dream -> death; friends still deny ('not some supernatural revenge story'). Mason starts typing 'Then Jason might on(ly be the first)' - hard cut before send.
Days later, lock-screen ping from Tariq in a private chat: he now believes - Lucas is dead too, same way.
Tariq (former skeptic) itemises Lucas's death, admits it's no coincidence, panics; Mason dismisses telling police.
Mason proposes going back to the graveyard to undo it; Tariq agrees: 'Today.' 'Alright.'
Typewriter prose: the grave has vanished entirely; nothing left to fix; days later both die in their sleep too.
'The end' - no CTA, no next-video tease.

pacing.re_hook_interval_s: time-skip cards at 148s and 350s; lock-screen jump at 551s; prose card at 776s - roughly every 200 s; deaths at 380s (46%) and 597s (72%)
pacing.notes: Read-along pace: each bubble lands ~3.4 s after the last (Mason's are preceded by letter-by-letter typing in the input bar, ~1.5-3 s; others by a grey typing-dots bubble ~1 s). The screen auto-scrolls one bubble at a time so the visual changes every few seconds although there are only ~9 true cuts. Music bed loops a ~3.5 min ambient track (RMS swings -28 to -16 dB) with no stingers at the twists. 46 s of prose epilogue at the end is typed faster (~210 wpm) than the chat.

art_style: Pixel-faithful iOS 10-era iMessage UI (white background, blue #1C8BF6-ish sent bubbles, light grey received bubbles, sender name above first bubble of a run, small circular photo avatars for each friend, camera/App Store icons + 'iMessage' input bar, 'Delivered' receipt, status bar with dots signal + battery %). Title/epilogue cards: black with white condensed sans caps (cards) or centred serif (prose).
techniques_worth_copying: Notification cold open: start on a lock screen with the most loaded line of the opening exchange as a banner - instant 'you're reading someone's phone' hook with zero narration.
Typing-in-input-bar before POV messages and grey typing dots before others - cheap, constant micro-motion that paces reading and builds anticipation.
Skeptic chorus that gets picked off in order: the friend who says 'nothing is gonna happen' dies first, the loudest skeptic (Tariq) becomes the convert who delivers the second death.
Rule-of-three escalation with explicit time-skip cards (THE NEXT MORNING / THE NEXT DAY / lock-screen days later) - each card is a re-hook.
ALL-CAPS bubbles reserved for panic moments ('GUYS I HAD A TERRIBLE DREAM', 'HE'S DEAD') - typographic volume change in a silent format.
Unsent-message cliffhanger: cut while the POV is still typing ('Then Jason might on|') straight to a lock-screen ping days later.
Group chat -> 1:1 chat switch to show the group has shrunk; avatars in the header literally show who's left.
Battery % and clock drift (89% -> 60%, 4:23 PM -> 8:15 AM) as subtle environmental storytelling.
Prose epilogue on black with typewriter reveal to deliver the unseen ending the chat format can't show (the vanished grave).
weaknesses_vs_outliers: Premise (graveyard dare, die in sleep) is a stock trope with no specific detail - no name on the grave, no date, no image.
Very repetitive dialogue (the 'it's just a dream' argument is run three times) - ~13 min for ~5 min of story.
No sound design keyed to events (no message pop, no stinger at deaths) and no visual horror inserts (photos, voice notes, unknown sender).
Thumbnail and title give no horror cue; low 480p-equivalent resolution (360x424 source).
Ending is told in prose instead of shown in the chat, and there's no CTA or series hook.
code_only_remake_needs: Remotion iMessage component kit: status bar (time, signal dots, battery %), header with stacked circular avatars + group name / single letter avatar, bubble list with sent/received styles, sender label on first bubble of a run, 'Delivered' receipt, timestamp separators ('Today 9:05 AM'), input bar with camera/App icons.

Message timeline schema: [{t, sender, text, caps?, typing_ms}] -> auto-layout bubbles with text wrapping (max width ~70%), auto-scroll so the newest bubble sits above the input bar, spring pop-in per bubble.
Typing simulation: letter-by-letter text in the input bar for the POV sender (variable speed, blinking caret), then send -> bubble; grey three-dot typing bubble for other senders.
Lock-screen scene: big thin clock + date, wallpaper (use an SVG/gradient or procedurally generated silhouette instead of a stock photo), notification banner slide-in.
Black title cards (condensed caps) and typewriter prose cards (serif, centred, per-character reveal at ~13 chars/s).
Avatars: generated flat SVG faces/initial circles rather than real photos.

Audio: royalty-free or synthesized ambient drone loop + optional message 'pop' SFX and low stinger at deaths (improvement over reference); no TTS required, though an optional TTS narration lane could raise retention.
Render at 1080x1920 (Shorts) or 1080x1350/1920x1080 with the phone frame centred - the reference's 360x424 is a quality gap we can beat.
transcript_source: No subtitles/auto-subs; audio is music only (faster-whisper small on a 120 s sample returned one spurious word). Transcript read visually from frames sampled every 4 s (all 227 bubbles captured; times +/-2 s). Full text in research/library/transcripts/0xzpKw7To98.txt.
